sample_unit: readmissions (each reviewed by two physicians and the AI)
models_evaluated: LLM-based agentic AI readmission review workflow

links.outcome: Blinded quality ratings of AI reviews versus physician reviews of the same readmissions
links.effect: Overall quality 4.35 (AI) vs 4.20 (physicians); mean difference 0.15, 95% CI -0.20 to 0.48; p=0.49; factuality and usefulness ratings also similar.
links.quote: Blinded overall quality ratings were similar for AI and physician reviews (4.35 vs. 4.20 on a 1-5 scale; mean difference 0.15, 95% CI -0.20 to 0.48; p=0.49), as were factuality/support and usefulness/actionability ratings.

links.outcome: Blinded physician evaluators rating AI review quality and factuality
links.effect: Blinded physician evaluators rated AI and physician reviews similarly on quality; no AI hallucinations were identified during factuality review.
links.quote: No AI hallucinations were identified during factuality review.

unlisted_practices: Using agentic AI to screen hospital readmissions for quality-improvement themes

screen.reason: Empirical retrospective evaluation comparing an agentic LLM chart-review system to physician chart reviewers for 30-day hospital readmissions, evaluated blindly by clinicians.
